info.title: Conversations API
info.description:
Create and drive a text conversation between an AI agent and a patient, then retrieve its outcome.

**New here?** Start with the [Integration Guide](./guide.html) — environments (Safety Portal / UAT / Production), minting a token, the end-to-end flow with `curl` examples, and the event-handling rules. This page is the field-by-field reference.

**Typical flow**

1. `POST /v1/conversations` — start a conversation for an `agent_id` / `script_id` / `patient_id`. You get back a `conversation_id` and the agent's opening `greeting`.
2. `POST /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages` — send the patient's message and receive the agent's reply, plus any `events` raised during that turn.
3. `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` — fetch current status and full message history (with events replayed) at any time, including after the conversation has ended.
4. `POST /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/end` — end the conversation and receive its `call_disposition`.
5. `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/transcript` — fetch the turn-by-turn transcript of an ended conversation.

**Authentication** — every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens are OAuth 2.0 client-credentials access tokens issued to your integration during onboarding (issuer, audience, `client_id` and `client_secret` are provided then). Read endpoints require the `read:chat_messages` scope; write endpoints require `write:chat_messages`. All data is scoped to the partner the token was issued to — a conversation, patient, script or agent that belongs to another partner is reported as not found.

**Concurrency** — keep at most one in-flight `POST .../messages` per conversation. A second concurrent send is rejected with `409 message_processing_busy`; retry it after the first completes.

**Events** — the `events` array on a message response is the signal channel for things the client UI should react to: an `escalation` being detected / evaluated / resolved, a `transfer_to_human`, or an `end_call`. Each event object carries a `type` discriminator. The same events are replayed on `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` so a client that lost a response can recover them. See the `Event` schema for the exact shapes and the rules for handling them.

**Errors** — failures return `{ "error_code", "message" }` (see `ConversationError`). `error_code` is a stable machine-readable string; `message` is human-readable and may change. Two exceptions: authentication failures (`401`, `403` from the bearer token itself) return the HTTP status with no JSON body, and a malformed `conversation_id` returns `400` with `{ "error": "..." }`.

**Retries** — `409 message_processing_busy` and `503` responses are transient; back off and retry. Use `idempotency_key` on sends so a retry after a lost response returns the original reply instead of running a new turn.

_Generated from the service's OpenAPI source and verified against the implementation on 2026-09-14._

tags.name: conversations
tags.description: Start, drive, inspect, and end AI agent conversations.

post.description:
Starts a new conversation between an agent and a patient using a given script, and generates the agent's opening greeting before responding. Expect a few seconds of latency — the reply is not returned until the conversation is fully ready to accept messages.

The patient must already exist for your partner (created through the patient ingestion API) before a conversation can be started for them; an unknown `patient_id` returns `404 patient_not_found`.

Requires scope `write:chat_messages`.

201.description: Conversation created and ready for messages.

400.description: `unsupported_script_configuration` — the referenced script uses a configuration this API cannot run as a text conversation.

401.description: Missing, expired or invalid bearer token. No response body.

403.description: Token lacks the `write:chat_messages` scope (no response body), or `missing_partner` — the token carries no partner identity.

404.description: `patient_not_found` — no patient with this `patient_id` exists for the authenticated partner.

409.description: Reserved for conflicts with existing state. Not emitted by the current implementation.

422.description: Request body failed validation (missing or wrongly typed field).

500.description: `prerequisite_data_unavailable` (patient, script or agent data could not be loaded), `preparation_failed`, or `llm_conversation_creation_failed`. Nothing was created; the request may be retried.

post.description:
Sends the patient's next message and returns the agent's reply for that turn, along with any `events` emitted while processing it. Send only the new utterance — the server holds the full history.

One turn at a time: a send that arrives while another is still processing is rejected with `409 message_processing_busy`. Once the conversation has ended (by `POST .../end`, or because an `end_call` event was emitted), further sends are rejected with `409 conversation_not_active`.

Supply an `idempotency_key` so a retry after a lost response is answered with the original reply instead of running a new turn.

Requires scope `write:chat_messages`.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Identifier returned by `create_conversation`. Must be a UUID.

200.description: The agent's reply for this turn.

400.description: `message_invalid` — `text` is empty or otherwise unacceptable. Also returned (as `{ "error": "..." }`) when `conversation_id` is not a valid UUID.

401.description: Missing, expired or invalid bearer token. No response body.

403.description: Token lacks the `write:chat_messages` scope (no response body), or `missing_partner`.

404.description: `conversation_not_found` — no such conversation for the authenticated partner. `conversation_runtime_unavailable` — the conversation exists but cannot be resumed.

409.description: `conversation_not_active` — the conversation has ended. `message_processing_busy` — another turn is in flight; retry shortly. `duplicate_message` — this `idempotency_key` was already used and the original turn did not complete successfully. `idempotency_key_reused` — this `idempotency_key` was already used with different `text`.

422.description: Request body failed validation (missing `text`, or `text` is blank).

500.description: `message_processing_failed` or `preparation_failed` — the turn could not be completed. The message may or may not have been recorded; check `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` before resending.

503.description: `conversation_runtime_unavailable` or `server_shutting_down` — the conversation cannot be served right now. Transient; back off and retry.

get.description:
Returns the conversation's current status and its full message history, with each turn's `events` replayed in the same shape as the send-message response. Served from durable storage, so it works at any point in the conversation's life, including after it has ended.

Use this to recover from a lost `send_message` response, to rebuild UI state, or to read the `call_disposition` of an ended conversation.

Requires scope `read:chat_messages`.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Identifier returned by `create_conversation`. Must be a UUID.

401.description: Missing, expired or invalid bearer token. No response body.

403.description: Token lacks the `read:chat_messages` scope. No response body.

404.description: `conversation_not_found` — no such conversation for the authenticated partner.

500.description: `history_replay_failed` — stored events for this conversation could not be rendered.

post.description:
Ends an active conversation and returns its `call_disposition`. After this call, further `send_message` requests are rejected with `409 conversation_not_active`.

Ending an already-ended conversation is idempotent and returns `200` with the same disposition.

Requires scope `write:chat_messages`.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the conversation to end. Must be a UUID.

401.description: Missing, expired or invalid bearer token. No response body.

403.description: Token lacks the `write:chat_messages` scope (no response body), or `missing_partner`.

404.description: `conversation_not_found` — no such conversation for the authenticated partner.

409.description: `message_processing_busy` — a turn is still in flight; retry shortly and the end will be applied.

500.description: `conversation_end_failed` — the conversation could not be ended. Retry, then check `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` for its status.

503.description: `conversation_runtime_unavailable` or `server_shutting_down` — transient; back off and retry.

get.description:
Returns the turn-by-turn transcript of an **ended** conversation. Transcript messages do not carry `events`; use `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` when you need those.

Requires scope `read:chat_messages`.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the conversation whose transcript to fetch. Must be a UUID.

401.description: Missing, expired or invalid bearer token. No response body.

403.description: Token lacks the `read:chat_messages` scope. No response body.

404.description: `conversation_not_found` — no such conversation for the authenticated partner.

409.description: `conversation_not_ended` — the conversation is still active. End it first, or use `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` for live history.

bearerAuth.description: OAuth 2.0 client-credentials access token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Obtain it from the token endpoint provided at onboarding using your `client_id` / `client_secret`; tokens are short-lived, so refresh on `401`. Because this flow uses a client secret, mint tokens only from a trusted backend or server-side environment. Scopes: `read:chat_messages` for GET endpoints, `write:chat_messages` for POST endpoints.

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: Identifier of the agent that will run the conversation. Provided at onboarding.

script_id.title: Script Id
script_id.description: Identifier of the script the agent should follow. Provided at onboarding.

patient_id.title: Patient Id
patient_id.description: Your external identifier for the patient — the same value supplied when the patient was ingested. The patient must already exist for your partner.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: Identifier for the newly created conversation. Use it in all subsequent calls.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: When the conversation was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

greeting.text: Hi, I'm your care assistant. How have you been feeling since your last visit?

text.title: Text
text.description: The agent's opening message to the patient. Display it as the first assistant message.

text.title: Text
text.description: The patient's new message. Must not be blank. Send only the new utterance — the server holds the full history.

idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key
idempotency_key.description: Opt-in retry key — mint a new value for each message; values must be unique within the conversation. A retry carrying the same key never re-runs the turn: if the original completed successfully, its response is returned again unchanged, otherwise the retry is rejected with `duplicate_message` (409). Reusing a key for different `text` is a client error and is rejected with `idempotency_key_reused` (409) rather than replayed, so a new message is never silently answered with an earlier reply. Once the conversation has ended, retries are rejected with `conversation_not_active` (409) like any other message; use `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` to recover a lost final response. Blank values are treated as absent.

example.text: I've had a headache since this morning.

SendMessageResponse.title: SendMessageResponse
SendMessageResponse.description: The agent's reply for one turn, plus the events that turn produced.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: Identifier of the agent's reply message. Matches `message_id` in `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` history.

events.title: Events
events.description: Client-visible events emitted for this turn, in emission order. Empty for most turns. Multiple distinct events are allowed, but `transfer_to_human` never repeats.

examples.text: I'm sorry you're dealing with that. How would you rate the pain from 1 to 10?
Would it be okay if I ask a few questions to better understand what you shared?
Thank you for answering those questions. I've completed the evaluation.
I'll help connect you with a human representative now.

events.context_summary: Patient reports a persistent fever and requires a human handoff.

examples.text: Thank you for chatting with me. This conversation is now complete.

status.title: Status
status.description: `active` while the conversation can accept messages; `ended` once it has been ended by the client, by the agent (`end_call` event), or by expiry.

call_disposition.title: Call Disposition
call_disposition.description: Present only for ended conversations, and may lag briefly after ending while the disposition is persisted. Same values as `EndConversationResponse.call_disposition`.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: When the conversation was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

patient_id.title: Patient Id
patient_id.description: Your external identifier for the patient, as supplied when the patient was ingested.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: Messages exchanged so far, in chronological order, each with the events replayed for its turn.

messages.text: Hi, I'm your care assistant. How have you been feeling since your last visit?
I've had a headache since this morning.
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. How would you rate the pain from 1 to 10?

Message.title: Message
Message.description: A single message in a conversation.

role.title: Role
role.description: `user` for the patient's messages, `assistant` for the agent's.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: When the message was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

HistoryMessage.title: HistoryMessage
HistoryMessage.description: A history message plus the replayed events for the turn it completed. Events use the same wire shape as `SendMessageResponse.events` and attach to the turn's final assistant message (falling back to the user message when the turn produced no assistant reply). A turn that emitted nothing has `events: []`.

events.title: Events
events.description: Replayed client-visible events for this message's turn, in emission order.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the conversation is being ended. Two values are recognised and recorded distinctly: `expired` (the client's own inactivity timeout fired) and `logged_out` (the patient signed out). Any other string is recorded as a regular user-initiated end.

call_disposition.title: Call Disposition
call_disposition.description: How the conversation concluded. Values: `call_completed`, `call_hung_up`, `no_answer`, `failed_verification`, `call_failed`, `immediate_hang_up`. Treat unknown values as opaque — the set may grow.

disposition.description: Reserved for a structured triage summary. **Not populated by the current implementation** — the field is omitted from responses today. Clients must not depend on it.

Disposition.title: Disposition
Disposition.description: Structured triage outcome of a conversation. Declared in the contract for forward compatibility; not populated by the current implementation.

status.title: Status
status.description: Lifecycle status of the conversation. Always `ended` on a successful transcript response.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: Turn-by-turn messages in chronological order. Transcript messages carry no `events`.

messages.text: Hi, I'm your care assistant. How have you been feeling since your last visit?
I've had a headache since this morning.

Event.title: Event
Event.description:
A client-visible event raised during a turn. Discriminate on `type`; `escalation` events additionally carry a `status`.

**Handling rules**

- **Escalations are not a fixed three-step sequence.** Each `status` is emitted at most once per evaluation and only when the evaluation reaches it. `in_progress` means the evaluation needs another turn, so an evaluation that resolves in a single turn reports `completed` alone, and one that never asks a follow-up skips `in_progress` entirely.
- **Not every escalation gets a `completed`.** An evaluation that is displaced by a higher-priority concern reports nothing further. Do not block UI state on a terminal event for every `escalation_id` you have seen.
- **`escalation_id` repeats.** It identifies the concern, not the occurrence. If the same concern is evaluated again later, the id is reused and a new lifecycle runs. Treat the latest event for an id as its current state — an earlier `TIER_0` is not a permanent all-clear.
- **`end_call` closes the conversation server-side.** After it, sends return `409 conversation_not_active`. Nothing else closes the conversation implicitly: a `transfer_to_human` does not end the session and is not followed by an `end_call`.

EscalationDetectedEvent.title: EscalationDetectedEvent
EscalationDetectedEvent.description: Emitted when a possible escalation is detected, unless its evaluation resolves in the same turn.

escalation_id.title: Escalation Id
escalation_id.description: Opaque identifier for the concern that escalated. Match it exactly; do not parse it or require UUID formatting. It repeats if the same concern is evaluated again later in the conversation, so treat the latest event for an `escalation_id` as its current state.

EscalationInProgressEvent.title: EscalationInProgressEvent
EscalationInProgressEvent.description: Emitted when the escalation evaluation needs another turn to resolve.

escalation_id.title: Escalation Id
escalation_id.description: Opaque identifier for the concern that escalated. See `EscalationDetectedEvent`.

EscalationCompletedEvent.title: EscalationCompletedEvent
EscalationCompletedEvent.description:
Emitted when the evaluation produces an outcome.

Not every escalation reaches it. One the system never adjudicates — because a higher-priority concern resolved first — stops at whatever status it last reported, so a missing `completed` is not an evaluation still running.

escalation_id.title: Escalation Id
escalation_id.description: Opaque identifier for the concern that escalated. See `EscalationDetectedEvent`.

tier.description: Outcome tier. `TIER_0` means the evaluation completed without a clinical escalation; `TIER_1` (least serious) through `TIER_4` (most serious) grade one that did. Match the token exactly — the set is a closed vocabulary, not a scale to parse or sort.

EscalationTier.title: EscalationTier
EscalationTier.description: Terminal outcome of an escalation evaluation. Strings rather than integers because `TIER_0` is not a degree of severity — it reports that the evaluation finished without a clinical escalation — so the set is a closed vocabulary rather than an ordered scale to do arithmetic on.

TransferToHumanEvent.title: TransferToHumanEvent
TransferToHumanEvent.description: Emitted at most once per conversation, when the agent hands the patient to a human. The conversation is not ended by this event; it remains open unless the client ends it or an `end_call` is emitted.

escalation_id.title: Escalation Id
escalation_id.description: Present when a reported escalation caused the transfer; otherwise omitted.

context_summary.title: Context Summary
context_summary.description: Hand-off context for the receiving human. May be empty when no summary is available. When populated it may contain sensitive conversation data and is not a verified clinical fact.

example.context_summary: Patient reports a persistent fever and requires a human handoff.

EndCallEvent.title: EndCallEvent
EndCallEvent.description: Emitted once when the server ends the conversation. After this event, further sends return `409 conversation_not_active`.

reason.description: Why the conversation ended. The current implementation emits `completed` for a normal end and `error` for an end state it cannot map; `expired`, `client_ended` and `transferred_to_human` are declared for clients to handle but are not emitted today.

ConversationError.title: ConversationError
ConversationError.description: Standard error body. `error_code` is stable and safe to branch on; `message` is for humans and may change. Codes in use: `missing_partner`, `patient_not_found`, `conversation_not_found`, `conversation_not_active`, `conversation_not_ended`, `conversation_runtime_unavailable`, `conversation_end_failed`, `prerequisite_data_unavailable`, `llm_conversation_creation_failed`, `preparation_failed`, `unsupported_script_configuration`, `server_shutting_down`, `message_processing_busy`, `message_processing_failed`, `message_invalid`, `duplicate_message`, `idempotency_key_reused`, `history_replay_failed`. Treat unknown codes as a generic failure for the returned HTTP status.

message.title: Message
message.description: Human-readable detail. Not stable; do not parse.

InvalidIdentifierError.title: InvalidIdentifierError
InvalidIdentifierError.description: Returned with `400` when a path `conversation_id` is not a valid UUID. Note the different shape from `ConversationError`.

ValidationError.title: ValidationError
ValidationError.description: Returned with `422` when a request body fails schema validation. A list of individual field errors.

loc.title: Location
loc.description: Path to the offending field, e.g. `["text"]`.

example.msg: Value error, text must not be empty
